entries.title: Amos 2:4
segments:
Judah; from the six idolatrous nations the prophet passes to Judah, on his way to Israel, to which latter kingdom he was especially sent. 
 
  Their lies; their idols and the whole system of idolatrous worship. it should be carefully noticed that while the prophet rebukes the gentile nations for sins against the dictates of natural religion, he specifies in the case of Judah only their despising the divine law and imitating the idolatry of their fathers; because, where a nation enjoys the light of revelation, the rejection of this is the sum of all rebellion and wickedness. 
 
vv 4-5. 
 
The rejection of God's revealed word is the most heinous sin of which a nation can be guilty; and it leads to the shameless practice of every iniquity.

entries.title: Amos 2:6
segments:
Israel; the prophet, having reached Israel, proceeds to enumerate at length the sins of both rulers and people. 
 
  They sold the righteous; creditors sold the righteous poor who were their debtors.  Compare

. 
 
  A pair of shoes; that is, a trifling sum. 
 
vv 6-8. 
 
Cruelty, fraud, and licentiousness cling together as kindred vices. They who make merchandise of the poor and defenceless for gain, may be expected also to oppress and defraud as they have opportunity, and to indulge themselves in shameless impurities.

entries.title: Amos 2:7
segments: Pant after the dust--the poor; are eager to spoil the poor man, so that he shall cover his head with dust as a sign of mourning,
; or, as some suppose, grudge him even this handful of dust.

entries.title: Amos 2:8
segments: Upon clothes laid to pledge; deposited by the borrower as pledges of payment.  Such pledges were to be returned at sunset.

Altar; idolatrous altar. 
 
  The wine of the condemned; wine purchased with the money of those whom they have unjustly fined, thus uniting oppression and drunkenness with idolatry.

entries.title: Amos 2:9
segments: Yet destroyed I the Amorite; the most powerful people of the Canaanites, living on both sides of the Jordan.

vv 9-11. 
 
The distinguished mercies conferred by God upon a people in times past, greatly aggravate the guilt of present unfaithfulness.  Let the people of the United States remember this, and humble themselves before God in view of present abounding wickedness.

entries.title: Amos 2:11
segments: Nazarites; a class of men particularly consecrated to God, some for life, and some for a limited time.  During the period of their consecration they were forbidden to drink wine or strong drink, or eat any produce of the vine.  See
.  Samson and Samuel were Nazarites from their birth.

entries.title: Amos 2:12
segments:
vv 12-16. 
 
To corrupt the professors of godliness, and suppress their testimony against sin, is the main effort of wicked men; but if they succeed in this, they will destroy both themselves and those who yield to their wishes.  God cannot be changed, nor his judgments upon the wicked hindered by ignorance and delusion.

entries.title: Amos 2:13
segments: Pressed under you; weary with bearing the load of your sins.
